statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-85790 (GHSA-2mxg-prvg-9jfg) is a .NET information disclosure issue in Microsoft QUIC (MsQuic), fixed by an updated native MsQuic library. Microsoft lists only Windows as affected, with Microsoft.Native.Quic.MsQuic.Schannel, the Windows Schannel build of MsQuic, as the affected package (versions before 2.5.12, and 2.6.0 before 2.6.3), and the .NET 10.0.13 release notes list this CVE (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2mxg-prvg-9jfg, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/470, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). On Windows, msquic.dll ships with the .NET runtime; on Linux, .NET uses a libmsquic installed separately from the system (https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/networking/quic/quic-overview). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. It has twelve builds published by 2026-11-28 (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0), each of eleven packages per architecture. We unpacked nine of its eleven packages in every build for x86_64 and aarch64: dotnet10-runtime, dotnet10-runtime-dbg, dotnet10-targeting-pack, dotnet10-apphost-pack, dotnet10-hostfxr, dotnet-host, aspnetcore10-runtime, aspnetcore10-runtime-dbg and aspnetcore10-targeting-pack; they hold no zip, nupkg or tar.gz archive. They hold managed .NET assemblies (every PE file has a CLR header), debug symbol files, and ELF programs and libraries that each have a dynamic section (the runtime's native libraries, the dotnet host, hostfxr, and the apphost, singlefilehost and libnethost.so in the apphost pack); the apphost pack also holds one static archive, libnethost.a, holding the .NET nethost library's objects. None of them contains a native Windows PE file, a Mach-O file, an MsQuic library (msquic.dll or libmsquic) or the Microsoft.Native.Quic.MsQuic.Schannel package, and no ELF file lists libmsquic as a needed library; the only file names containing Quic are the managed System.Net.Quic and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Transport.Quic assemblies and their symbol and documentation files. Of the two build-input packages, we unpacked dotnet10-runtime-artifacts for x86_64 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0 and 10.0.13-r0 and aarch64 10.0.2-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0, and dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap for x86_64 10.0.2-r0 and aarch64 10.0.10-r0, recursing into the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: in each of them every PE file is a managed .NET assembly and there is no Mach-O file, so none carries the native Windows msquic.dll that the Schannel package ships; the artifacts packages hold no ELF file at all, and in the 10.0.2-r0 x86_64 bootstrap package no file name contains msquic and no ELF file lists libmsquic as a needed library. We did not unpack the artifacts and bootstrap packages of the other builds. No package of any published build declares a dependency on libmsquic in the repository index. The managed System.Net.Quic.dll loads a system libmsquic at run time when one is installed, and is not the affected component.

CVE-2026-85790 (GHSA-2mxg-prvg-9jfg) is a .NET information disclosure issue in Microsoft QUIC (MsQuic), fixed by an updated native MsQuic library. Microsoft lists only Windows as affected, with Microsoft.Native.Quic.MsQuic.Schannel, the Windows Schannel build of MsQuic, as the affected package (versions before 2.5.12, and 2.6.0 before 2.6.3), and lists the fix in the .NET 8.0.32 release (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2mxg-prvg-9jfg, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/470, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). On Windows, msquic.dll ships with the .NET runtime; on Linux, .NET uses a libmsquic installed separately on the system (https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/networking/quic/quic-overview). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. None of them contains an MsQuic library (msquic.dll or libmsquic) or the Microsoft.Native.Quic.MsQuic.Schannel package, none of them contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file, every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly with a CLR header, and no package declares a dependency on libmsquic. They carry the managed System.Net.Quic.dll, which loads a system libmsquic at run time and is not the affected component.
